source.title: Decoding Partial Differential Equations: Cross-Modal Adaptation of Decoder-only Models to PDEs
source.authors: Paloma Garc'ia-de-Herreros; Philipp Slusallek; Dietrich Klakow; Vagrant Gautam

record.tranche_reason: The study varies model parameter count and measures PDE-task performance, using nRMSE rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy. This bears on downstream predictability under scaling, but not the original pretraining-loss measurement.
record.gate_note: The study reports scale-sweep nRMSE results for cross-modal PDE adaptation. These bear on V6, which concerns downstream performance with scale. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws to loss curves, or optimize parameter/token allocations. Results about Parallel Flipping and Sequence Doubling as methods are not treated as scaling results.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps pretrained GPT-2 (137M–1.61B) and Pythia (14M–1.4B) sizes and measures downstream nRMSE after cross-modal fine-tuning on PDE tasks. It explicitly asks whether scaling helps 'as seen in other areas (Kaplan et al.)'. This is a new setting (cross-modal transfer) with a direct result on V6, downstream improvement with scale. It fits no power laws and does not measure pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that scaling decoder-only models does not help: it barely narrows the gap to encoder-only models, and gains are small, irregular and task-specific. They attribute the gap to unidirectional attention rather than size. Even with their bidirectionality methods, they still do not see consistent scaling behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps pretrained model sizes in cross-modal PDE adaptation and measures downstream nRMSE. It does not measure language-model pretraining cross-entropy, vary training tokens or compute, or fit the original scaling-law relationships.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by PDE task, model family, and adaptation method (ORCA versus FPT).

fits_no_version.finding: At similar size (~110–160M), encoder-only models beat decoder-only models on downstream PDE nRMSE, often by an order of magnitude, with ORCA on three of four tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture type (encoder vs decoder attention) strongly affects downstream cross-modal transfer at fixed size.

record.problems: The measured outcome is PDE-task nRMSE rather than held-out language-model loss. Results cover four 1-dimensional PDE datasets and two cross-modal adaptation methods; the paper cautions against generalizing to other PDE tasks and notes possible proxy-dataset reproduction issues and adaptation instability.
record.rows_left_out: The model-size sweep also includes Diffusion-Sorption results shown in Figures 3 and 7, but those values are figure-only and were not extracted within the 60-row cap after prioritizing the numerical scale-sweep tables. Tables 4–6 also report Parallel Flipping and Sequence Doubling results at each size; those method-comparison cells are omitted because they assess the introduced adaptation methods rather than the original setup's scaling result. The paper's aggregate textual statements about these results are summarized in authors_conclusion.

untested.parts: Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss; any predictive fit of downstream error against scale. Diffusion-Sorption scale results are figure-only and not in the rows.
Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Shape effects on pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds for transfer or fine-tuning loss. No fits are made.

record.verdict_notes: Downstream measure is cross-modal fine-tuned PDE nRMSE with only 4–6 sizes per family and no fits, so evidence on 'predictable' scaling is qualitative. Proxy-dataset replication issues and checkpoint randomness are possible confounds noted by the authors. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether small-run power-law fits predict the loss of much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Whether architecture details change language-model pretraining loss only slightly at fixed parameter count.
The study uses PDE data for cross-modal adaptation, but measures task nRMSE rather than whether a power-law form holds for loss in another modality or training regime.
The study varies model size and evaluates downstream PDE performance. It does not test downstream performance against pretraining loss or establish predictive fits.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, or analysis of fitting-method dependence.

relationships.condition: ORCA on Advection (both families); FPT GPT-2 on Advection and Navier-Stokes
relationships.reason: Larger models give higher nRMSE than the smallest model, e.g. GPT-2 XL ORCA Advection 0.542 vs 0.508 and FPT Navier-Stokes 0.829 vs 0.703 (R03, R04, R08–R10, R32–R34, R53, R54).
relationships.display_finding: Larger models had higher nRMSE, including GPT-2 XL ORCA Advection at 0.542 versus 0.508 and FPT Navier-Stokes at 0.829 versus 0.703.

relationships.condition: ORCA on Navier-Stokes and Diffusion-Reaction; FPT on Pythia (all tasks) and on GPT-2 Diffusion-Reaction
relationships.reason: Error falls with scale but non-monotonically and modestly: best-vs-smallest gains are 5% (GPT-2) and 12% (Pythia) on ORCA Navier-Stokes, with outliers and dips (R12–R14, R16–R20, R22–R30, R36–R40, R42–R44, R46–R50, R56–R60).
relationships.display_finding: Errors declined unevenly, with best-versus-smallest improvements of 5% for GPT-2 and 12% for Pythia on ORCA Navier-Stokes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Advection with ORCA or FPT original setup; selected larger models compared with the smallest model in each family
reader_labels.reason: Several larger models have worse nRMSE than the smallest model, including GPT-2 812M and 1.61B with ORCA and GPT-2 sizes 380M–1.61B with FPT (R03–R04, R32–R34); Pythia also worsens at several larger ORCA sizes (R08–R10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the tested PDE tasks, model families, and adaptation methods
reader_labels.reason: The scale trends vary by task and adaptation: some sequences improve, others are non-monotonic or worsen, so the results do not show a uniformly predictable downstream scaling pattern (R02–R30, R31–R60).
